title: SCM_RIGHTS installs an FD before publishing its number
mechanism: FileMessage::write_to inserts each received file into the file table before writing its descriptor number to the control buffer. A fault on that write is turned into MSG_CTRUNC by ControlMessage::write_all_to and the inserted entry is not removed.
contract: A descriptor received through SCM_RIGHTS is installed only after its complete number has been copied to the control buffer (Linux receive_fd in fs/file.c, scm_detach_fds in net/core/scm.c).
observed: Source only: the file is inserted into the table first, and a fault on the number write leaves it installed while recvmsg succeeds with MSG_CTRUNC. MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC is not applied.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an SCM_RIGHTS receive whose descriptor slot sits on a PROT_NONE page, comparing the open-descriptor set before and after.

caveats: Source-only lead: installed/unpublished ownership and control flags need runtime verification. A source comment shows the ordering was a known upstream choice. MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC alone is an unsupported-flag question, not a confirmed bug.
